title: India Isn't Playing at the World Cup. It Might Be the Tournament's Biggest Audience Anyway.
excerpt: With 305 million football fans, Bollywood on European club feeds, and 300 million streaming viewers, the diaspora and India's digital-first generation are reshaping how the world sells the beautiful game — all without a team on the pitch.
body:
As the FIFA World Cup 2026 enters its knockout phase across stadiums in the United States, Mexico, and Canada, one of the tournament's most invested audiences doesn't have a team to cheer for.

India has never played at a World Cup. And yet, the country has quietly become Instagram's second-largest football audience globally, trailing only Brazil. FIFA's official Instagram account counts more than 10 percent of its followers from India. Cristiano Ronaldo alone has an estimated 81 million Indian followers. Lionel Messi has 56 million. Combined, the two icons command an Indian audience approaching 140 million people — larger than the populations of most countries that actually qualified.

The numbers suggest something that goes far beyond casual interest. India's football audience, by the Ormax estimate, now stands at around 305 million people, making football the country's second-largest sport after cricket.

## The Clubs Have Noticed

Over the past few months, the global Instagram feeds of Europe's biggest football clubs have begun looking surprisingly Indian. Not translations. Not subtitled clips. Actual cultural references.

La Liga's account used a 1988 Marathi song to spotlight its stars. Borussia Dortmund's feed, as one observer put it, "now reads like a Bollywood account that also posts football." Liverpool has been sharing game clips and player reactions against the backdrop of viral Indian songs. Manchester City ran a post featuring Erling Haaland set to a Hindi serial-style music score — it became a fan favourite.

Tottenham runs a dedicated @Spurs_India account. La Liga's English handle has posted Diwali greetings written entirely in Hindi. The Premier League India's official meme account has recast viral Indian cricket moments as football tributes rather than simply translating content.



> **""What's notable is that these aren't translations," BestMediaInfo noted in a recent analysis."**


"What's notable is that these aren't translations," BestMediaInfo noted in a recent analysis. "They are references. And that points to a broader shift in how global brands are approaching India."

The Premier League reported 144.5 million followers in India and attracted 7.1 crore viewers during the 2023-24 season — a 63 percent increase over the previous year.

## The Broadcaster Windfall

For Zee Entertainment, which is airing the World Cup on its Unite8 Sports channels and ZEE5, the tournament has produced dramatic numbers. The company said its sports portfolio crossed 300 million unique reach across linear, digital, and social platforms since June 1. Unite8 Sports added 60 million new viewers during the tournament period.

Zee said it recorded 17 percent higher live reach than the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar during the same period — despite the late-night kick-off times in Indian Standard Time. Six new advertisers, including Lenovo, Adidas, Ceat, and JBL, signed on as the tournament enters the knockout rounds, joining existing sponsors Mahindra, Apple, and Pernod Ricard.

Unite8 Sports 2 has emerged as the leading English sports channel in India during the tournament window.

## The 'Diaspora World Cup'

The tournament itself has a diaspora story running through it. About one in four of the 1,248 players at this World Cup was born outside the country they represent — up from 16.8 percent in Qatar 2022. Some have called it the "Diaspora World Cup."

Cape Verde, the smallest country ever to reach a World Cup knockout round, has 15 players in its 26-member squad who hold a second nationality — six born in the Netherlands, four in Portugal, three in France. The team held both Spain and Uruguay to draws in the group stage before drawing 0-0 with Saudi Arabia to qualify for a historic Round of 32 meeting with Argentina.

Iraq's Zidane Iqbal, born in Manchester to a Pakistani father and Iraqi mother, was named after the French football legend Zinedine Zidane. Japan's standout goalkeeper Zion Suzuki was born in the United States to a Japanese mother and Ghanaian father. Switzerland's Granit Xhaka has Kosovar immigrant parents. The tournament's opening goal was scored by Mexico's Julian Quinones, who was born in Colombia and naturalised in 2023.

For the Indian diaspora in North America, the tournament is unusually accessible. Group-stage and knockout matches are being played in Houston, Dallas, the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Los Angeles, Philadelphia, and Seattle — all cities with significant NRI populations. The Round of 32 kicks off on Sunday, June 28, with South Africa versus Canada at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, followed by marquee clashes: Brazil versus Japan (Houston), USA versus Bosnia and Herzegovina (Bay Area), and Argentina versus Uruguay (Dallas).

## What It Means for the Diaspora

The World Cup has always been a cultural event for NRIs. This time, it is also a local one. With 16 of the 48 group-stage matches played in the five US states with the highest Indian-American populations, the tournament is, for the first time, genuinely on the diaspora's doorstep.

Analysts argue that social media has done more for football fandom in India than any broadcaster could. "For years, broadcasters believed they were the driving force behind fandom," RevSportz noted. "What Instagram's numbers reveal is that the equation has changed. Social media has been steadily building football fandom in India. Imagine what will happen the day the nation finally qualifies for the World Cup."

The question, perhaps, is no longer whether India is a football country. It is whether anyone can afford to treat it as anything else.

*The FIFA World Cup 2026 knockout rounds begin Sunday, June 28. All matches are broadcast on Unite8 Sports and ZEE5 in India.*
